correctness.rationale: Uniform proof: reciprocal summability makes G entire and gives H(T)=exp(o(T)); double zeros of G yield a perturbation bounded by epsilon B_j times the strictly positive angular gap e^{s_j}-|exp(w)|, with sup B_j finite and epsilon B<1/2. Hence exactly n global maximizers on every prescribed circle. Taylor coefficient at z is epsilon nonzero; upper bound exp(r^n)+epsilon r exp(o(r^n)) and exact values exp(r_j^n) give order n and type one. The explicit summable sequence s_j=(j+1)log^2(j+2) gives the R^n/log^2 R lower-count bound. All quantifiers and boundaries are handled analytically.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The present theorem fixes first gap one and prescribes exactly n simultaneous radial maxima on every radius from an arbitrary reciprocal-summable infinite family, with exact order n, normal type one, and a concrete R^n/log^2 R lower count. Theorem 1.1 of the 2026 finite-order paper proves unbounded maxima on some radii but imposes none of these simultaneous prescriptions or densities. Theorem 1.2 prescribes individual points with different moduli. The 2020 finite prescription concerns discontinuities/singletons, not exact n-point maxima on infinitely many circles. Li bounds the complementary generic-circle cardinality; no implication to this construction.

value.rationale: Answers a motivated question left by a fresh first-gap generic-bound theorem: how large and how freely positioned can its exceptional radius family be under fixed Taylor gap and controlled growth? Provides a uniform infinite prescribed-circle interpolation theorem with exact multiplicities and normal type, plus near-order quantitative density. This is more than reproducing already-known finite-order existence or a small finite-example increment.
